title: Cargo
subtitle: Multi-crate workspaces, feature-gated builds and a carve gate that keeps product crates free of estate-specific imports.

stats.label: crates in Agent Swarm, split into a product zone and an estate zone
deploy modes besides the full run: dry-run, local-only, skip-build

lede: AgentOS is a Rust Cargo workspace that ships a manifest of binaries. I wanted one deploy path that nobody, human or agent, could get half right, in place of ad hoc copy steps across a multi-crate estate. Deployment is a single Cargo verb, cargo deploy , built with the xtask pattern as a workspace member and wired in through a Cargo alias. Agent Swarm splits its crates into product-zone crates and estate-specific ones. I wanted the runtime separable from the estate it grew up in, so a scripted carve gate fails the check when a product-zone crate imports anything platform-specific.
quote: Carve gates and dependency firewalls are checks that fail the build; a README cannot enforce architecture.
evidence: Build and release engineering: one deploy verb for a 546,000-line Rust workspace of 19 members, publishing binaries by atomic symlink swap so nothing launches a half-written file.
Architecture enforcement in the build: a carve gate across 23 crates that fails the check when a product crate imports estate-specific code, and a CI firewall keeping CUDA out of a storage daemon.
author: Corey James
